sections.description:
Settlement of Disputes (first elections) Rules 1962
Settlement of Disputes (first
elections) Rules 1962
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 1st May 1962]
No.
F. 1 (17)/62-Els.-In exercise of the powers conferred by Article 37 of the
Settlement of Disputes (First Elections) Order, 1962 (P. O. No. 13 of 1962),
the Election Commission is pleased to make the following rules :
1. Short title and commencement. (1) These rules may be called the Settlement of
Disputes (First Elections) Rules, 1962.
(2)
They shall come into force at once.
2. Definitions. In these
Rules unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context----
(a)
"article" means an article of the Order ;
(b)
"Order" means the Settlement of Disputes (First Elections) Order,
1962 (P. O. No. 13 of 1962).
3. Appeals. (1) An appeal under Article 5
shall be addressed to the Election Commission and if there is no Election
Commission in existence to the Chief Election Commissioner and shall be filed
with the Secretary Election Commission or the Regional Election Commissioner at
Lahore or llaeca as the case
may be,
(a) within
7 days of the date of the decision of the Returning Officer under clause (4) of
Article 13 of the National and
Provincial Assemblies (First Elections) Order, 1962 (P. O. No. 4 of 1962), if
it is against an order of rejection of a nomination paper ; and
(b) within
7 days of the date of declaration of result by the Return ing Officer under
clause 1 (a)
of Article 39 of the National and
Provincial Assemblies (First Elections) Order, 1962 (P. O. No. 4 of 1962) if it
relates to any proceedings under Article 37 of the said order, and in such a
case, the date of the count and the facts and reasons on which the result is
challenged as well as the relief sought shall be stated in the memorandum of
appeal.
(2)
The memorandum of appeal shall be accompanied by a certifi cate to the effect
that a copy of the same has been delivered to each of the candidates concerned.
(3)
The deposits accompanying each appeal shall be made in the name of the
Secretary to the Election Commission or the Regional Election Commissioner
concerned and shall be made in the manner provided by rule 4 of the National
and Provincial Assemblies (First Elections) Rules, 1962.
4. Presentation
of election petitions. An election petition shall be
presented under clause (a) of Article 9 by being delivered in person to the
Secretary or the Deputy Secretary to the Election Commission or to the Regional
Election Commissioner of the area in which the constituency concerned lies.
5. Deposits.--The sum of Rs. 500.00 to be deposited as security for costs with each
election petition shall be deposited in the name of the Secretary to the
Election Commission in the manner provided by rule 4 (3).of the National and
Provincial Assemblies (First Elections) Rules, 1962.
6. Statement
of case by Tribunal. An application
to the Tribunal under Article 28 of the order by any of the parties for making
a reference to the Election Commission shall be made within 3 days of the date
on which the point of law is raised for the first time before the Tribunal.
7. The
withdrawal of respondents. A notice
under Article 32 of the order by a respondent in an election petition shall be
in the form of an affidavit affirming that the signatory is a respondent and
that he has no intention to contest the petition.
